scenarios.title: Extended blackout
scenarios.description: The power grid is down for an unknown period. Internet and mobile networks may be unreliable.
triage_questions: Is anyone injured, unwell, or reliant on powered medical equipment or refrigerated medicine?
Can you smell gas or smoke, or see fallen power lines nearby?
Is anyone using a generator, barbecue, camp stove or fuel heater indoors or in a garage?
Is it dangerously hot or cold where you are right now?
Do you have safe drinking water and a way to receive official updates (radio)?

steps.text: Check everyone is safe. If anyone's life is at risk, call emergency services (000 in Australia).
Rule out carbon monoxide and fire risks: no fuel-burning devices indoors; torches instead of candles.
Turn on the battery/wind-up radio for official updates; put phones on low-power mode.
Unplug sensitive appliances; leave one light switched on to know when power returns.
Keep fridge and freezer shut; eat perishable food first, then pantry food.
Count drinking water and set a daily allowance per person (don't under-drink).
Set up one room for warmth or cooling and check on vulnerable household members and neighbours.
Set up sanitation if water pressure fails (bagged toilet, hand hygiene station).
Review the household plan daily: supplies remaining, health, official advice.

scenarios.title: Food & supply disruption
scenarios.description: Shops are closed or empty for an extended period.
triage_questions: Does anyone have urgent medication or dietary needs that will run out first?
How many days of water and food do you currently have?
Are there infants or pets with special food requirements?

steps.text: Inventory water, food (kcal), medication and hygiene supplies.
Prioritise medication and infant needs; contact your pharmacist early.
Plan meals by energy, eating perishable items first.
Maintain hygiene and sanitation to prevent illness.

scenarios.title: Natural disaster / isolation
scenarios.description: Storm, flood or bushfire has cut roads and services. Follow official warnings first.
triage_questions: Is there an active warning or evacuation order for your area?
Is your home structurally safe and free of floodwater or fire risk?

steps.text: Check official warnings (e.g. Emergency WA) and follow evacuation orders immediately.
Call emergency services for injuries or people trapped.
Grab the emergency kit and documents if you need to leave.
Make water safe if supply may be contaminated.

scenarios.title: Zombie apocalypse (FICTIONAL SIMULATION)
scenarios.description: A training game. Real skills — planning, rationing, communication — wrapped in fiction. Not real-world guidance.
triage_questions: Who is in your survivor group and what skills does each person bring?
How many days of water and food can you carry vs. store?
What is your rally point and backup rally point?

steps.text: [Simulation] Inventory your real supplies — the game uses your actual household data.
[Simulation] Agree on rally points and communication signals.
[Simulation] Plan a rebuild objective: restore light and radio using the electricity tech tree.
